samplingMethod: Python random.Random(20261029).sample over sorted populations of passed lines, in order exercises(70 of 661), stories(50 of 424 sentences), reception(25 of 177: readings, non-word clips, scenario partner/terminal lines), explanations(15 of 166: concept vi fields + guidebook ### sections); lines/objects named in es-vi-answers.jsonl or es-vi-language.jsonl excluded. Script: scratchpad/audit/sample.py

findings.proposed: ["Es un perro", "Un perro", "Esto es un perro", "Eso es un perro"]
findings.reason: Speech grading is exact whole-utterance match (src/lib/speech/grader.ts). Asked 'Hãy nói đây là gì' with a picture, 'Esto es un perro' is the most common learner answer and is correct, yet rejected. The typeAnswer twin un-l3-e4 already accepts 'Eso/Ese es un perro'.

findings.current: Cerrado el lunes. Entrada: ocho euros.
findings.proposed: Cerrado los lunes. Entrada: ocho euros.
findings.reason: A standing opening-hours notice states a habitual closing day: 'los lunes' (or 'Lunes: cerrado'). 'Cerrado el lunes' reads as 'closed this coming Monday' and models the wrong article for a recurring day, which the course itself teaches (los martes y jueves). Same pattern in es.read.cp3_aviso_biblioteca ('Cerrado el domingo y el lunes'), which the review touched for agreement only.

findings.current: Con esta medicina, la fiebre va a pasar pronto.
findings.proposed: Con esta medicina, la fiebre se va a pasar pronto.
findings.reason: With an illness or symptom 'pasar' is pronominal ('se pasa', 'se te pasa'); non-pronominal 'la fiebre va a pasar' sounds like a calque of 'the fever will pass' (same family as es-lg-56 'Dos días pasan' and es-lg-61 'La canción pasa', which were fixed). 'la fiebre va a bajar pronto' is equally natural.

findings.locator: content/courses/es-vi.json es-vi:unit-b guidebook §4 (Ir a — tương lai gần)
findings.proposed: **ir** (đi): *voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van* (*vais* = các bạn đi, ngôi *vosotros* dùng ở Tây Ban Nha).
findings.reason: The course model is Peninsular and VARIETY.md says paradigms carry the vosotros forms; the guidebook lists the five-form Latin-American paradigm, as do the ser/estar and hablar/comer/vivir lines of the same guidebook (§1, §3: no sois/estáis/habláis/coméis/vivís). After the review the stories now use vosotros (¿Tenéis hambre?, ¿Queréis sopa?, vuestro profesor), so learners meet forms the guidebook implies do not exist. No guidebook mentions vosotros at all.

findings.proposed: Tôi có một anh trai (hoặc em trai).
findings.reason: Same issue as es-lg-10 (fixed in the unit-4 guidebook): hermano covers older and younger brother; fix not propagated to this exercise.

findings.current: Cho tôi một cà phê, làm ơn.
findings.proposed: Cho tôi một ly cà phê nhé (làm ơn).
findings.reason: Sentence-final 'làm ơn' is a calque of 'please'; natural Vietnamese ordering is 'Cho tôi một ly cà phê ạ/nhé'. Kept as P2 because the blank drills por favor = làm ơn.

findings.proposed: ["La tienda está abierta", "La tienda ya está abierta", "La tienda está abierta ahora"]
findings.reason: Only one exact variant for a semantic prompt ('đang mở cửa' invites 'ya'/'ahora'); exact matching makes the item brittle.

findings.current: Por la mañana trabaja en la tienda.
findings.proposed: Por la mañana trabaja en una tienda.
findings.reason: First mention of the shop; the definite article presupposes a known shop.

findings.current: Ana ríe y no llora más.
findings.proposed: Ana se ríe y ya no llora.
findings.reason: 'ya no' is the natural 'no longer'; 'se ríe' is the usual Peninsular form.

findings.current: Sí, voy a la casa de mis padres.
findings.proposed: Sí, voy a casa de mis padres.
findings.reason: Peninsular usage drops the article in 'a/en casa de + person' (the review fixed 'en la casa' → 'en casa' in es-lg-49 but did not generalise). Same pattern: la_sopa_de_la_abuela[1], la_abuela_y_el_movil[17], la_cancion_de_ines[0].

findings.current: En la casa de Inés hay un bebé, Leo.
findings.proposed: En casa de Inés hay un bebé, Leo.
findings.reason: See previous: 'en casa de' without article is the Peninsular norm.

findings.current: Lola lleva música y Iván lleva las bebidas.
findings.proposed: Lola lleva la música y Iván, las bebidas.
findings.reason: Article-less 'lleva música' sounds clipped next to 'las bebidas' (same reasoning as fixed es-lg-28).

findings.current: Khách sạn nằm trước mặt biển.
findings.proposed: Khách sạn nằm ngay trước biển.
findings.reason: 'trước mặt biển' is an awkward collocation in Vietnamese.

findings.current: Después de la clase, las diez personas de la clase van a un bar.
findings.proposed: Después de la clase, los diez compañeros van a un bar.
findings.reason: Repetition of 'la clase' in one sentence.

findings.current: El café de la estación abre a las siete.
findings.proposed: La cafetería de la estación abre a las siete.
findings.reason: In Spain the station's café is 'la cafetería'; 'el café' reads first as the drink.

findings.current: solo cuatro personas, ¿vale? / Perfecto, entonces somos cuatro.
findings.proposed: solo tres o cuatro personas, ¿vale? / Perfecto, entonces somos tres.
findings.reason: Only Marta, the speaker and Jorge are mentioned, so 'somos cuatro' does not add up; no exam item depends on the count.
'¿Algo más?' / '¿Alguna cosa más?' is the standard shop-counter question in Spain.
Closing an exam just finished: Peninsular Spanish uses the present perfect; bare 'Terminamos' is curt.

findings.current: me gusta + một thứ; me gustan + nhiều thứ; động từ hợp với thứ được thích.
findings.proposed: me gusta + một thứ; me gustan + nhiều thứ; động từ chia theo thứ được thích.
findings.reason: 'hợp với' is a calque of 'agrees with'; 'chia theo' is the Vietnamese grammar term used elsewhere in the course.

appliedFixProblems.problem: Transcript now reads 'Llueve mucho, coge el paraguas.' but src/content/reception/es-listening.json still has 'lleva paraguas' and es.clip.dele_a_l1_03 still points at the mp3 rendered from the old text (assets/audio/es-reception/711c94dda11a3d3555ff.mp3). Applies to every applied transcript/story/partner-line/speech-target fix: content:compile and an audio regeneration run are needed before the fix reaches learners, otherwise the audio contradicts the text (content:check should fail until then).

Fix is correct Peninsular Spanish (¿Queréis sopa?, with ¿Tenéis hambre? from es-lg-53), but no guidebook introduces vosotros forms (see es-au-4), and sentence[1] of the same story still has 'a la casa de su abuela' (the es-lg-49 'en casa' rule was not generalised).
Alternative 'el andén dos.' is now redundant because dictation ignores punctuation; harmless.
